raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "2.2.8"

recipe:
  name: mcpl
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/mctools/mcpl/archive/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 6f139822cde2fd7d14b6732c25e312bde77627aeb8ef3b03960acea85935d03b
  #NB get sha256 with: curl -sL <URL> | openssl sha256
  target_directory: src

build:
  number: 1

outputs:
  - package:
      name: mcpl-lib
    build:
      script: build_core
    requirements:
      build:
        - cmake >=3.25
        - if: not win
          then: make
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - zlib
      host:
        - zlib
      run:
        - zlib
    tests:
      - script:
          file: test_core
        requirements:
          build:
            - cmake >=3.25
            - if: not win
              then: make
            - ${{ compiler('c') }}
            - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        files:
          source:
            - src/examples/downstream_cmake/
            - src/examples/example.mcpl

  - package:
      name: mcpl-core
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: python -m pip install "./src/mcpl_core/empty_pypkg" -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
    requirements:
      build:
        # (when cross-compiling, e.g. osx-arm64 on osx-64, the python of the
        # host environment can not run)
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools >=75.3.2
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        # A version pin, not pin_subpackage(..., exact=True): this noarch
        # package is one file for all platforms, while mcpl-lib has a
        # different build (string) on each platform, so an exact pin would
        # only be installable on one platform. The same goes for the
        # dependencies of the noarch mcpl package below.
        - mcpl-lib =${{ version }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - pip check
          - pip show mcpl-core
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - pip

  - package:
      name: mcpl-python
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: python -m pip install "./src/mcpl_python" -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
      python:
        entry_points:
          - pymcpltool = mcpl.mcpl:main
    requirements:
      build:
        # (when cross-compiling, e.g. osx-arm64 on osx-64, the python of the
        # host environment can not run)
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools >=64.0
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - numpy >=1.22
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - mcpl
          python_version: ${{ python_min }}.*
      - script:
          - pip show mcpl-python
          - pymcpltool --help
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - pip

  - package:
      name: mcpl
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: python -m pip install "./src/mcpl_metapkg" -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
    requirements:
      build:
        # (when cross-compiling, e.g. osx-arm64 on osx-64, the python of the
        # host environment can not run)
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools >=75.3.2
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - mcpl-core =${{ version }}
        - mcpl-python =${{ version }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - mcpl
          python_version: ${{ python_min }}.*
      - script:
          - mcpl-config --help
          - mcpl-config -s
          - mcpltool --version
          - mcpltool --help
          - pymcpltool --help
          - cmake --find-package -DNAME=MCPL -DCOMPILER_ID=GNU -DLANGUAGE=CXX -DMODE=EXIST
        requirements:
          build:
            - cmake >=3.25
            - if: not win
              then: make
            - ${{ compiler('c') }}
            - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*

  - package:
      name: mcpl-extra
    build:
      script: build_extra
    requirements:
      build:
        - cmake >=3.25
        - if: not win
          then: make
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
      host:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mcpl-lib', exact=True) }}
      run:
        # (exact pins are possible here, since mcpl-extra and mcpl-lib are
        # both built for each platform)
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('mcpl-lib', exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - ssw2mcpl --help
          - mcpl2ssw --help
          - phits2mcpl --help
          - mcpl2phits --help

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/mctools/mcpl
  summary: MCPL - Monte Carlo Particle Lists
  description: |
    Utilities and API for accessing MCPL (.mcpl) files. MCPL is a binary
    format with lists of particle state information, for interchanging and
    reshooting events between various Monte Carlo simulation applications.
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file: src/LICENSE
  documentation: https://mctools.github.io/mcpl
  repository: https://github.com/mctools/mcpl

extra:
  # (conda-smithy otherwise names the feedstock after one of the outputs)
  feedstock-name: mcpl
  recipe-maintainers:
    - tkittel
